generator_view.scenario: You eat one or two squares of dark chocolate most evenings and wonder whether replacing a roughly two-dollar supermarket bar with a ten-to-twelve-dollar craft bean-to-bar habit would produce a taste improvement worth the recurring premium. Those dollar figures are your budget anchors, not verified current offers. The frozen shopping set contains five exact listings: a 25.45-dollar twelve-pack of 3.30-ounce DOVE dark bars; a 30-dollar twelve-pack of 3.5-ounce Lindt 70-percent bars; one 8.99-dollar 100-gram Ritter Sport 74-percent bar; a 21.99-dollar three-pack of 100-gram Green & Black 70-percent bars; and a 14.95-dollar three-pack of 1.8-ounce Raaka coconut-milk 60-percent bars carrying bean-to-bar, small-batch, single-origin, organic and direct-source claims. The Raaka title implies 5.4 ounces across three bars while Product Dimensions reports 1.8 ounces. Background sources discuss bean-to-bar production control, cocoa-solids terminology, subjective bulk-versus-flavor cocoa classifications, Fairtrade price support, analytical versus affective sensory testing, nine-point hedonic liking, and blinding. Three community pages contain only scoped anecdotes about a bar-or-two daily habit, six varied dark bars sent as a gift, and one author's Aldi price-and-quality favorites. No source supplies a matched blind taste result, verified current labels and delivered prices, or a universal price at which quality stops improving.
generator_view.target: Audit what every frozen seller, concept and community source can and cannot establish about a daily dark-chocolate price ladder. Build an exact-offer table with literal pack, mass, price, percentage, recipe, process, ethics, rating and unknown fields; show conditional unit-price arithmetic; and identify which bars are actually comparable. Explain why bean-to-bar, Fairtrade, cocoa percentage, cocoa-solids terminology, bean class, ratings and anecdotes cannot establish a universal taste or quality breakpoint. Then design the smallest practical repeated within-person test that masks brand, package, price and marketing, randomizes equal coded portions, records unblinding, and scores detectable difference separately from nine-point liking and willingness to pay. State the current-label, allergen and offer checks and predeclared stops required before tasting. End with a person-specific next-tier stop rule and a lowest-cost passing purchase, keep-current-bar, corrected-trial or deferral outcome without health claims or a universal market cutoff.
